name: gitlab-mcp
description: GitLab over MCP from your own account: issues, merge requests, reviews, the repository and CI.
long_description:
Work inside GitLab projects from your own gitlab.com account: find and read issues and merge requests, review a merge request, read the repository and CI. Content from GitLab is marked as untrusted data rather than instructions. Nothing this server writes runs a quick action, code reaches a protected branch only through a merge request, and merging, approving, running CI and deleting are not offered unless you turn them on.

THIS BUNDLE DOES NOT LOG YOU IN, and cannot. Each person brings their own OAuth application, so before the tools work you need to register one on gitlab.com and run `gitlab-mcp login --client-id <application id>` once from a terminal. The setup is documented at https://github.com/mmedum/gitlab-mcp/blob/main/docs/setup.md. Without that step the server starts, lists its tools, and answers every call with "not signed in".

client_id.title: OAuth application id
client_id.description: The id of the OAuth application you registered on gitlab.com. You still need to run `gitlab-mcp login --client-id <application id>` once from a terminal.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: Which stored login to use. Separate profiles keep separate tokens, such as one per GitLab account. Leave it empty for the default profile.

read_only.title: Read-only
read_only.description: Register only the read tools and use a read_api token, so GitLab itself refuses a write. Needs a login made in read-only mode. It cannot be combined with Merging, approving, CI and releases, or with Deleting and making issues public: the server then refuses to start.

enable_ship.title: Merging, approving, CI and releases
enable_ship.description: Register the tools that merge, approve and rebase merge requests, apply review suggestions to a branch, move an issue to another project, run, retry, play and cancel CI, and, with the releases toolset, create releases. Off by default, and not with Read-only. This server asks nobody before a call, so Claude Desktop's approval of each tool is then the only check.

enable_destructive.title: Deleting and making issues public
enable_destructive.description: Register the delete tools and make_issue_public. Each call also needs confirm: true, and nothing deleted comes back. Off by default, and not with Read-only.

toolsets.title: Optional toolsets
toolsets.description: Comma-separated toolsets to add: activity, deployments, planning, releases, snippets, wiki, or all. Leave it empty for none.

write_namespaces.title: Write only to
write_namespaces.description: Comma-separated groups or projects that every write is confined to, such as my-group, other-group/project. Leave it empty and writes reach every project your account can write to.

upload_dirs.title: Image directory
upload_dirs.description: A dedicated folder upload_file may read images from, such as a screenshots folder: it can read every image in it. Your home folder and a disk's root are refused. Leave it empty and upload_file refuses every path.
